articles.title: Nouveau driver gets patches for HDMI Deep Color support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: New patches posted to the dri-devel mailing list add HDMI Deep Color support to Nouveau, the open-source NVIDIA Linux kernel driver, enabling 10, 12, or 16 bits per color channel. The patches currently support only RGB, and 16-bit output is untested on capable displays.

articles.title: OpenShot video editor now officially available as a snap
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: OpenShot's official snap package went live on the Canonical Snap Store on 22 September, installable on all supported Ubuntu releases. It eases installation and brings newer versions to older LTS users, though sandbox permissions for microphone, camera, and removable media must be granted manually.

articles.title: Linux 7.2 vs. Linux 7.3 Shows A Few Improvements With AMD Strix Halo
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarked Linux 7.3 against 7.2 on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo Framework Desktop after Ubuntu 26.10 switched kernels. Most real-world workloads were unchanged, but NUMA performance improved significantly, network latency dropped slightly, and a few graphics and micro-benchmarks saw small gains.

articles.title: KDE Picks Enterprise, Documentation, and Styling as New Goals
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: KDE has chosen three community goals for 2026–2028: making Plasma viable for enterprise and managed deployments, overhauling its fragmented documentation, and building a next-generation styling system via the Ocean design system and Union theming engine.

articles.title: Ubuntu wiki gets its first overhaul in 16 years
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Canonical has launched a rebuilt Ubuntu Wiki, its first major update since 2010, now running on MediaWiki. The new wiki is smaller and aimed at Ubuntu users rather than contributors, replacing an aging Python 2 stack with security vulnerabilities.

articles.title: PeppermintOS switches from Xorg to XLibre, avoiding Wayland
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: PeppermintOS is replacing the stalled xorg-server with XLibre, an X11 fork, in its upcoming ISO refreshes, and says it has no plans to move to Wayland. Testing has gone well so far, but XLibre is controversial: Artix Linux adopted it as default, then reverted after heavy bug reports and harassment of a developer.

articles.title: Survey: Organizations increasingly adopt OpenSearch for AI workloads, not just search
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: A Linux Foundation Research and OpenSearch Software Foundation report, based on 294 respondents surveyed in May 2026, finds OpenSearch awareness at 89% and production deployments doubled to 36% in two years. Among users, 62% run AI workloads on it, with cost and vendor independence driving adoption.

articles.title: NetBSD 10.2 Released With New Hardware Support and Security Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: The NetBSD Project has released NetBSD 10.2, the second point release in the still-supported NetBSD 10 stable branch. It adds hardware support including Realtek RTL8126 5Gbps Ethernet, fixes security issues in IPFilter and TCP timestamps, and updates OpenSSL to 3.0.21 and Xorg to 21.1.24.

articles.title: Compiling the kernel with gccrs
articles.author: daroc
articles.brief: Talks at RustConf 2026 and Kangrejos covered the status of gccrs, the Rust frontend for GCC, with a focus on compiling the Linux kernel. The project is making good progress, but the compiler remains far from usable for that goal.

articles.title: Security updates for Tuesday
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup lists security updates from AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Fedora 45 ships a large coordinated update touching ffmpeg, chromium, and many multimedia packages; Ubuntu fixes include the kernel, OpenJDK, glib2.0, and expat across multiple LTS releases.

articles.title: AMD BC-250 Linux support expands with PSP secure processor enablement patches
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: New kernel patches enable the AMD PSP Secure Processor on the BC-250, a cut-down PlayStation 5 APU board originally sold for crypto mining. The three-patch series updates the AMD CCP driver so the board's secure processor works for encryption tasks under Linux.

articles.title: Igalia Celebrates 25 Years of Linux and Open-Source Contributions
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Worker-owned consultancy Igalia, founded in September 2001 by University of A Coruña engineers, marks 25 years of open-source work. Now nearly 200 people, it contributes to the Linux kernel, WebKit, Chromium, Servo, Mesa, GStreamer, and LLVM, with recent projects for Valve and others.

articles.title: Linux perf script overhauled as fast Python C module
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A 49-patch series from Google engineer Ian Rogers replaces perf's embedded Python/Perl scripting with a standalone Python C extension module, cutting overhead and build dependencies. One script that took 3.7 seconds now runs in 0.1 seconds.

articles.title: Linux 7.3-rc4 Released: More Fixes Caught By LLMs, But Nothing Too Scary
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released Linux 7.3-rc4, a larger-than-usual rc with fixes spread across drivers, filesystems, and networking, many flagged by LLM-based defect hunting. Notable merges include x86 fixes, new XPad game controller support, two Btrfs bug fixes, and a fix for silent user-space data loss present since 2023.

articles.title: Important x86 Fixes Merged Ahead Of Linux 7.3-rc4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A batch of x86/x86_64 fixes landed in Linux 7.3 Git ahead of 7.3-rc4. They block problematic Intel Granite Rapids microcode that could cause machine check exceptions, fix Intel FRED on Panther Lake crashing games under Wine/Steam Play, and disable APX register use in -march=native kernel builds.

articles.title: Gzip 1.15 Released, Fixing Bugs Present Since Its Inception
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Gzip 1.15 is out, following version 1.14 from April 2025, with over a hundred commits focused on bug fixes. Several bugs existed since the tool's beginning, including a race that could remove the wrong file, a buffer overflow in LZH decompression, and use of uninitialized memory.

articles.title: KDE's 2026-2028 Goals: Enterprise Support, Better Docs, Next-Gen Styling
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At KDE Akademy 2026 in Graz, KDE announced its three community-voted goals for the next two years: improving Plasma for enterprise deployments, overhauling documentation, and building a next-generation styling system via the Ocean design project and Union theming engine.

articles.title: Starling 0.5 desktop adds optional walkable 3D waterfront city mode
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Starling, the Swift-written Wayland desktop developed largely with Claude Code, released version 0.5 with an optional 3D desktop mode rendering a walkable waterfront city where apps remain real windows. The release also adds Windows support via WSL2 with RDP display mode.

articles.title: Vulkan 1.4.363 Released With New VK_INTEL_device_info Extension
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Vulkan 1.4.363 is out with spec clarifications, fixes, and multi-instance VUs for DMA-BUF external memory. Its headline addition is VK_INTEL_device_info, an Intel vendor extension that exposes the graphics IP block version of Intel GPUs to applications.

articles.title: AMD Strix Halo Shows Performance Gains on Ubuntu 26.10, Especially with amd64v3
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarked a Framework Desktop with a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo chip on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS versus an Ubuntu 26.10 daily ISO, plus an amd64v3 package build. Ubuntu 26.10 reportedly performs better than 26.04 LTS, with extra out-of-the-box gains from the experimental x86_64-v3 packages.

articles.title: Fedora CoreOS 45 Test Week starts September 21
articles.author: Lukáš Růžička
articles.brief: The Fedora CoreOS and QA teams are running a Test Week starting September 21, 2026, inviting the community to test Fedora CoreOS based on Fedora 45 before it reaches testing and stable streams. Participants download test images, follow provided test cases, and report results on the wiki page.

articles.title: Fedora Linux Asahi Remix 45 Beta brings Fedora 45 to Apple Silicon
articles.author: Davide Cavalca
articles.brief: Fedora Asahi Remix 45 Beta is out, bringing Fedora Linux 45 Beta to Apple Silicon Macs ahead of general availability in about a month. It is the first Remix release with out-of-the-box support for M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max systems, though M3 GPU acceleration awaits a future Mesa update.
